Buying Tanko in Malaysia vs Importing Directly: A Sourcing Comparison

By Primaxs Marketing (M) Sdn Bhd · Exclusive Malaysia distributor for Tanko · Updated August 2026

Tanko is a Taiwan manufacturer, so a reasonable procurement question is whether to import directly or buy through the exclusive Malaysia distributor. The honest answer depends on what you're buying and how much, but for most Malaysian businesses the local route wins on total cost and time once the full picture is counted.

The headline price is not the landed cost

Direct import can show a lower unit price, but the number that matters is the total landed cost. Importing adds freight, insurance, customs duties and clearance, currency exposure, and the internal time to manage it all. By the time a directly imported cabinet reaches your floor, the apparent saving is usually much smaller than it looked — and sometimes gone.

FactorLocal distributor (Primaxs)Direct import
Unit priceRinggit, all-inLower headline, before add-ons
Freight & insuranceIncludedAdded, and variable
Customs & dutiesHandledYour responsibility
Currency riskNone — quoted in MYRExposed to FX moves
Lead time (stocked items)Local stock, fastShipping + clearance, weeks
Minimum orderFlexibleFactory MOQ may apply
Model selection helpLocal team who handled the rangeSelf-service from a catalogue
After-sales & warrantyAdministered locallyCross-border RMA

Direct answer: For most Malaysian buyers, sourcing stocked Tanko items through the local distributor is faster and comparable on total cost, with local support and warranty. Direct import only tends to make sense for very large, planned orders where factory MOQ and long lead times are acceptable.

Lead time is the quiet cost

A directly imported order is subject to production scheduling, ocean or air freight, and customs clearance — weeks at best, and exposed to delays outside your control. When a workshop needs a cabinet or bench this month, local stock is worth more than a small unit saving. For planned capital projects the timing is easier, but even then the coordination burden sits with you.

Support you can actually reach

When something needs a part, an adjustment or a warranty claim, the difference is stark. A local distributor resolves it through a Malaysia office. A direct import means dealing cross-border with the factory, shipping items back and forth, and managing the claim yourself in another time zone and language.

Choosing the right model the first time

Tanko's catalogue is deep, with many variants that differ by top material, drawer layout, holder interface and accessories. Choosing the wrong variant on a self-service import is an expensive mistake to unwind. A local team that has handled the range can steer you to the right configuration before you commit — which is why we build a page for every variant and quote to your actual specification.

When direct import might still make sense

  • Very large, single orders where factory MOQ is easily met.
  • Planned projects with long lead-time tolerance.
  • In-house logistics and customs capability already in place.

Outside those cases, the local route is usually the lower-risk, lower-total-cost choice.

Frequently asked questions

Is it cheaper to import Tanko directly from Taiwan?

The headline unit price can be lower, but once freight, insurance, customs, currency and your own management time are added, the total landed cost is usually comparable to buying locally — and lead times are much longer. For most Malaysian buyers the local route is the better value.

How long does direct import take versus local stock?

Directly imported orders are subject to production scheduling, freight and customs clearance — typically weeks, with delay risk. Stocked items from the local distributor are available far faster, which matters when a workshop needs equipment this month.

What about warranty if I import directly?

A direct import means handling any warranty claim cross-border with the factory, including return shipping and coordination in another time zone. Buying through the Malaysia distributor means the warranty is administered locally.

When does importing directly make sense?

Mainly for very large single orders that easily meet factory minimums, planned projects that can absorb long lead times, and buyers with in-house logistics and customs capability. Outside those cases, local sourcing is usually lower risk and lower total cost.
